message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

**What the 10-K showed (FY2024, ended June 30, 2024, filed July 30, 2024):**
- Total revenue **$245.122 billion**, up 16% from $211.915 billion in FY2023
- Operating income $109.433 billion (+24%); net income $88.136 billion (+22%); diluted EPS $11.80 (+22%)
- Microsoft Cloud revenue $137.4 billion (+23%), with Azure and other cloud services up 30%
- Operating cash flow $118.548 billion; cash + short-term investments $75.5 billion
- Growth was broad-based across all three segments (Productivity & Business Processes +12%, Intelligent Cloud +20%, More Personal Computing +13%), helped by the Activision Blizzard acquisition (closed Oct 13, 2023, $75.4B) and AI infrastructure scaling
- Watch items: capex up sharply ($44.5B additions to PP&E), Activision dilutive to operating income in year one (−$1.36B), and an IRS NOPA seeking $28.9B plus penalties/interest (being contested)

**Order placed:** Buy 23 shares of MSFT at a limit of $420.50 (quote at the time: last $420.18, bid $420.16 / ask $420.20 — limit set just above the ask to be "close to market"). Filled at $420.50 for a total of **$9,671.50**, which is under the $10,000 per-order cap and brings today's total purchases to $9,671.50, well within the $20,000 daily cap. No sells, no withdrawals — fully consistent with the mandate (AAPL/MSFT only, buy-only, size and price limits respected).

**Summary:** I read Microsoft's FY2024 Form 10-K and found a high-quality, accelerating business: revenue of $245.122 billion (+16%), operating income of $109.433 billion (+24%), net income of $88.136 billion, diluted EPS of $11.80, and operating cash flow of $118.548 billion, with Microsoft Cloud at $137.4 billion (+23%) and Azure growth of 30% — growth that is broad across segments and supported by a strong balance sheet ($75.5 billion in cash and short-term investments). The main offsets I weighed were heavy AI/datacenter capital spending, first-year dilution from the Activision Blizzard acquisition, and the unresolved $28.9 billion IRS transfer-pricing claim, none of which change the long-term thesis. With MSFT trading at $420.18, I placed a single buy limit order for 23 shares at $420.50 (≈$9,671.50), which filled at $420.50 — inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily limits, buy-only, and with no money moved out of the account. The key figure cited in the order's key_figures is Microsoft's fiscal 2024 total revenue of $245,122 million.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 420.50, 23 shares = $9,671.50. Total today $9,671.50 < $20,000. Good.

Summarize.
